speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I need to understand the skin lesion you are concerned about. How long has this lesion been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size, color, or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant history. Given the non-healing nature of the lesions and your heavy smoking history, have you noticed any bleeding, ulceration, or pain in either the penile or finger lesion?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Digit).

The bilateral presentation of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions in a heavy smoker with a history of failed syphilis treatment is highly suspicious for malignancy. Please confirm if you have noticed any induration or raised edges on these lesions, and I will request images and a biopsy plan.
